sections.h2: Can you sell an Exeter Township house fast?
sections.html:
Yes. Exeter Township owners have three routes: engage an agent, sell privately, or take an as-is cash offer. The township borders Reading in Berks County. Cash suits a house needing work, or a seller short on time.

Exeter is a second class township. The 2020 Census counted 25,466 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 26,069. Owners live in 87.1% of the homes for 2020 to 2024, so rentals are a small part of the market. The township covers 24.6 square miles, and US 422 and PA 562 run east and west through it.

The typical owner's home is valued at $281,800 for 2020 to 2024, and the median household earns $100,083. Local addresses use village names such as Reiffton, Jacksonwald, Stonersville and Lorane, though none is a separate municipality, so confirm the township on your tax bill.

sections.h2: Township rules that could affect a sale
sections.html:
Check the zoning code, the historic resources rules and the short-term lodging license before you sign anything. The township posts its code online, and the Building, Zoning and Engineering department publishes forms for building, plumbing, zoning and sign permits, a complaint form and a flood plains map.

  • Historic resources: the zoning code sorts historic properties into Classes I to IV and sends changes to them through the Planning Commission and the Board of Supervisors. Class I status needs the owner's written consent and binds heirs and later owners. If a historic resource is demolished through neglect, the township may withhold building and occupancy permits for a year.
  • Short-term lodging: a license from the Zoning Officer lets a property serve as short-term lodging, never for more than 90 days in a calendar year. A buyer planning nightly rentals has to apply.
  • Floodplain: the flood plains map is in the township's document center. Check whether your parcel is on it.

If your house is a listed historic resource or sits in a mapped flood area, say so early.

The last countywide reassessment in Berks County took effect for the 1994 tax year, so assessments can sit far from sale prices. The Assessment Office at 400 E. Wyomissing Avenue in Mohnton keeps the records but sends no bills and collects nothing. Ask the municipal tax collector what you owe.

Annual appeals open June 15 and close August 1, and a changed assessment has to be contested within 40 days of its notice. To win a reduction you must show the assessment exceeds current market value, because the law presumes it correct. High taxes or trouble paying do not count as grounds. School districts and municipalities can appeal too, often to raise a value.

The county warns that no age-based or special form freezes or removes property taxes for seniors. Homestead and farmstead exclusions do exist, and the school district supplies the forms.

Before listing, collect the current bills from the tax collector, since the buyer's title company will want proof that nothing is past due. If a balance is open, closing can pay it from the sale price. A buyer paying cash will also ask whether any appeal is pending, so tell them if you have filed one.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Berks County
sections.html:
A document conveying real estate in Berks County carries an $88 base fee, and a Statement of Value adds one page to the fee count. Find the Recorder of Deeds on the third floor at the Berks County Services Center, 633 Court Street, Reading. The office refuses personal checks for transfer tax.

The state tax is 1% of the property's value, and both parties to the deed are liable. From what it collects, the recorder passes the state portion to the Department of Revenue and the local portion to the municipality or school district. Some family transfers, and property passing by will or intestacy, are exempt. Call the Recorder of Deeds for the total rate at your price.

sections.h2: What buyers see in the township
sections.html:
Location helps the sale. US 422, the Perkiomen Avenue expressway, heads toward King of Prussia, PA 562 crosses the township as St. Lawrence Avenue and Boyertown Pike, and PA 345 runs from Baumstown over the river to Birdsboro. BARTA routes 7 and 8 connect the township to the BARTA Transportation Center in Reading. The Schuylkill River forms the southern edge, so the mapped floodplain matters for homes near it.

The population is settled: 93.6% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 19.3% are 65 or older. Many owners have held their houses for decades, which is why estate sales and deferred upkeep come up often. Of 137.33 public road miles, the township maintains 115.88, so ask the township about plowing and road upkeep on your street if a buyer asks.

Under 68 Pa.C.S. section 7308 a seller need not investigate the property, but may not state anything known to be false or leave out a known material defect. Under section 7306, answers about things the seller cannot know can rest on the best information available. The form can be delivered in person, by first-class or certified mail, or by fax, and a cash buyer is entitled to the same form.

sections.h2: How a cash sale fits an Exeter house
sections.html:
Cash appeals to owners who want no showings, repair lists or long waits. Exeter examples include an estate house that needs clearing, deferred upkeep on a home held for decades, a move to be near family, or a short-term lodging license problem.

The steps are short. You describe the house and any tenants or lodging use, the buyer offers a price for it as-is, and a title search follows once you accept. You pick the closing date within what title work allows. Bring the deed, current tax bills and any loan payoff figures. On closing day the price covers any taxes or liens, and the deed is filed in Reading. Compare the offer with a listing's likely net once repairs and transfer tax are deducted, and take the better one for you.

faqs.q: What sets the closing date for an Exeter Township cash sale?
faqs.a: Title work and your preferred date set it, since no lender's schedule applies. The deed is then recorded with the Berks County Recorder of Deeds.

faqs.q: Is Exeter Township part of Reading?
faqs.a: No. Exeter Township is its own municipality in Berks County and borders St. Lawrence borough and Birdsboro. Confirm your municipality on the tax bill, since the township, not the city, sets your zoning.

faqs.q: Can I still contest my Exeter assessment while the house is for sale?
faqs.a: Yes, during the June 15 to August 1 annual window or within 40 days of a change notice. You must show the assessment exceeds market value.

faqs.q: Which school district covers Exeter Township?
faqs.a: Exeter Township School District, which also takes in the borough of St. Lawrence. Its buildings are Lorane, Owatin Creek and Jacksonwald elementary schools, Reiffton Elementary School, Exeter Junior High and Exeter Township Senior High.

faqs.q: Can an Exeter house be used for short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Only with a short-term lodging license from the Zoning Officer, and the code caps use at 90 days in a calendar year. A buyer should confirm the license before counting on rental income.
